title: Independent depth shifts bounded by reported errors can reverse the Geysers shallow-share decline across 2014 in an M2+ catalog
abstract: We tested the depth sensitivity of a shallow-event share decline across a previously reported Geysers rate change. A fixed ComCat snapshot has 3,385 M2+ events in 2004-2013 and 2,398 in 2014-2025. The share at depth 1.5 km or less fell from 44.79% to 29.98%. If each depth can move independently by no more than its reported depth error, sharp limits on the later-minus-earlier share are -33.20 to +4.42 percentage points. Thus an allowed assignment can reverse the sign. The critical error multiple is about 0.786. At an M2.5 floor, the limits at one reported error are -31.39 to +2.58 points. Year and two-year resampling do not remove this sensitivity. These are conditional assignment bounds, not probabilities that depth errors caused the decline. Reported errors need not bound actual errors, and joint relocation constraints can exclude the adverse assignments. Same-source selection of the boundary, catalog changes and a rectangular region limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a scalar audit support reproduction. Raw events stay external.

display.caption: Sharp shallow-share change limits under independent bounded depth movements. Gray bars show conditional year-bootstrap outer envelopes. Depth-error caps are assumptions, not confidence levels.

citations.reason: Prior shallow-event rate result motivates the fixed boundary and depth cut. We test depth-error sensitivity, with overlapping source data.
Prior magnitude-share test motivates a distinct depth-composition test.
